short: A general who ruled England as head of state without ever taking the crown.
full:
Cromwell entered the Civil War as a Huntingdonshire member of Parliament with no military training and ended it as the New Model Army's most effective commander, victorious at Marston Moor, Naseby and Preston. He signed Charles I's death warrant, then subdued Ireland in a campaign whose storming of Drogheda and Wexford is still bitterly remembered, and beat the Scots at Dunbar and Worcester.

He dissolved the Rump Parliament by force in April 1653 and, after the nominated assembly that followed collapsed, was installed as Lord Protector under the Instrument of Government on 16 December 1653, a written constitution unique in English history. He governed with and without parliaments, briefly through eleven major-generals, readmitted Jews to England, and refused the crown when it was offered to him in 1657. He died on 3 September 1658. His son Richard lasted eight months, and the monarchy was restored in 1660.
